findings.claim: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Netflix reported revenue of $12.874 billion, up 12% from $11.510 billion, operating income of $4.459 billion and a 34.6% operating margin versus 28.2%, net income of $3.664 billion, and diluted EPS of $0.87 versus $0.59.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Netflix guided fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of $13.442 billion and a 26.0% operating margin, and full-year 2026 revenue of $51.1 billion, up 13%, with a 31.5% operating margin versus 29.5% in 2025; the full-year revenue figure is 0.2% below the midpoint of the prior forecast.

Netflix cut its 2026 advertising-revenue expectation to about $2.7 billion from about $3 billion because some ad-product capabilities rolled out more slowly than expected, and said the fourth-quarter margin guide includes about 120 basis points, and the full-year margin guide about 30 basis points, of drag from recently announced headcount reductions.

Third-quarter revenue growth of $1.364 billion included $1.057 billion of higher subscription revenue and $256 million of higher advertising revenue; for the nine months, advertising revenue increased $864 million.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In the third quarter Netflix repurchased 63,917,979 shares for $4.8 billion, and for the nine months 130,349,765 shares for $10.7 billion, excluding the 1% excise tax; $22.3 billion remained authorized after an additional $25 billion authorization in April 2026.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On July 22, 2026 Netflix completed a registered offering of $1 billion of 5.250% senior notes due 2036 and said the net proceeds are intended to repay its 4.375% senior notes due 2026 at maturity and for general corporate purposes.

At September 30, 2026 Netflix had $15.132 billion of notes outstanding, net of issuance costs and hedging adjustments, of which $2.475 billion was short-term, including $1.000 billion of 4.375% notes maturing in November 2026; the $3 billion revolver due April 12, 2029 and the commercial-paper program were undrawn, cash was $8.194 billion, and management said liquidity should cover needs for the next twelve months and beyond.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On February 27, 2026 Warner Bros. Discovery terminated the amended merger agreement so it could combine with Paramount Skydance, Paramount Skydance paid Netflix the $2.8 billion termination fee, Netflix recorded that fee in first-quarter interest and other income, and the related acquisition financing was terminated with nothing borrowed.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Content obligations were $25.223 billion at September 30, 2026, including $19.6 billion not yet on the balance sheet, and Netflix said unknown obligations for future titles beyond contractual minimums are expected to be significant.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Netflix lowered its 2026 free-cash-flow forecast to about $12.0 billion from about $12.5 billion, primarily because of a real-estate transaction it expected to close in the fourth quarter; third-quarter free cash flow was $2.9 billion versus $2.7 billion a year earlier.
Netflix said it will introduce its advertising tier in 15 new countries in 2027, with the first launches in March 2027 covering nine EMEA countries plus Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand.
Netflix said it secured a new licensing deal with Disney that includes all five Ice Age films, and that its summer partnership with French broadcaster TF1 is generating incremental viewing in France.

Netflix said member response to its 2026 price increases is consistent with prior price changes, while acknowledging investor concern about view-hours growth and saying it seeks to accelerate that growth.

On November 24, 2026 Netflix said it is purchasing Radford Studio Center in Los Angeles, will retain the existing studio team, and has engaged ZVantage's Backlot Studio Services, with Cinelease as the production-equipment provider.
findings.source_title: Deepening Our Commitment to Los Angeles: Netflix Purchases Radford Studio Center

findings.claim: Netflix said the litigation matters it did not list are not material individually or in aggregate, and that it is routinely audited on non-income taxes, mainly disputes over the tax treatment and tax rate applied to revenue in certain jurisdictions.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Netflix said third-quarter view hours in India grew 24% year over year, India revenue grew about 18% year over year on a foreign-exchange-neutral basis, and India delivered the company's largest quarter of paid net additions there.

upcoming_catalysts.event: First tranche of advertising-tier launches in nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand.
The $1.000 billion of 4.375% senior notes mature in November 2026.

policy_links.policy: Inflation Reduction Act 1% excise tax on stock repurchases
policy_links.bottleneck: cost of returning cash through buybacks
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The tax does not create Netflix revenue. The 10-Q reports the $4.8 billion third-quarter and $10.7 billion nine-month repurchase totals excluding that 1% excise tax.

key_risks.risk: 2026 advertising revenue is now expected at about $2.7 billion rather than about $3 billion because ad-product features are rolling out more slowly, and headcount reductions are guided to reduce fourth-quarter operating margin by about 120 basis points.
Content obligations were $25.223 billion at September 30, 2026, and commitments for unknown future titles beyond stated minimums are expected to be significant.

On February 27, 2026 Warner Bros. Discovery terminated the streaming-and-studios merger so it could combine with Paramount Skydance. Netflix received the $2.8 billion termination fee and the unused acquisition financing ended with nothing borrowed.

Non-income-tax authorities routinely dispute the tax treatment and rate applied to Netflix revenue in some jurisdictions, and an unfavorable material legal outcome could affect operations or liquidity.

notes: No at-the-market program, convertible issuance, or common-stock offering turned up in the last twelve months of filings reviewed. Netflix repurchased stock instead. The November 14, 2025 ten-for-one split is slightly outside the trailing twelve months; the 10-Q says share and per-share figures are presented after that split. The November 24, 2026 company post announces the Radford Studio Center purchase but does not state a price, so no price is included. The shareholder letter does not disclose how many jobs the headcount reduction covers. The letter's expected fourth-quarter real-estate closing is not explicitly tied by Netflix to Radford. No fourth-quarter earnings date was found. No going-concern language or delisting notice was found. The $1.0 billion 4.375% notes are disclosed as maturing in November 2026; no later filing in the submissions list through November 10 reports a default.
